A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IAC research work. Their complete main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Appendix F reports original IAC-versus-PLMLE simulations on four SBM scenarios, with means and standard deviations from 100 instances in Table 2 and boxplots in Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulations and additionally reports Model 4 runtimes and a DBLP co-authorship clustering study in Appendix F.1.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same trimming, spectral initialization, parameter estimation and iterative likelihood-based assignments. Fixing eight clusters in the new DBLP experiment is an evaluation setting, not a revision of the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from four synthetic SBM scenarios to include an observed DBLP co-authorship network with 246 researchers and 1,118 connections. This introduces real-network coverage beyond the retained model-generated data.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator remains the computationally lighter PLMLE, Algorithm 3 of Gao et al. (2017). The new runtime and DBLP comparisons use the same IAC–PLMLE pair.

E3.justification: The new DBLP evaluation fixes K=8 and examines community-size and publication distributions. v3 also adds elapsed-time evaluation for Model 4. The stated settings of the four original synthetic scenarios remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1 adds a real-network case study examining the communities produced by IAC and PLMLE through network visualizations, community sizes and publications per author. No new ablation or explicit robustness test is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 simulation instances, means, standard deviations and boxplots. The added runtime results include ± values but specify no new run count or statistical estimation procedure; they do not establish a change in reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 and Figures 1–4 retain their results. v3 newly reports Model 4 runtimes of 0.177 ± 0.037 seconds for IAC and 0.915 ± 0.752 seconds for PLMLE, plus DBLP clustering and community/publication distributions in Figures 5–6.

T1.justification: The divergence definition, assumptions (A1)–(A3), theoretical guarantees and proofs in Appendices B–E are unchanged. The Model 2 probability matrix is relocated from the former Appendix F.1 without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of instance-optimal recovery in expectation and with high probability, adaptation without known model parameters, and near-linear computational complexity. The new experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 newly identifies node-attributed SBMs as representing structures outside the present model and as a future extension. Appendix F.1 interprets IAC's DBLP partition as avoiding excessively small communities and producing a more continuous community-size distribution.

D1.justification: v3 documents DBLP construction using researchers with at least 20 publications from a 50,000-paper corpus and edges for at least one co-authored paper. It also supplies runtime measurements. The MATLAB/macOS hardware description and Model 2 probability matrix were already present and are merely relocated.

R1.justification: v3 adds Backstrom et al. (2006) for DBLP and Dreveton et al. (2023) for node-attributed SBMs, briefly extending the discussion of related models. The principal novelty and comparisons with earlier clustering research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized prose edits in Section 2.1 and Appendix F. Existing experimental details move into Appendix F, while F.1 becomes the real-data subsection. Acknowledgements, an impact statement, publication information and affiliation edits are added; the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figures 5–6 add paired network visualizations and community/publication statistics. Existing figures and algorithm displays are repositioned, with local page reflow. The original tables and four boxplots retain their content.

improvement.justification: The Model 4 timing comparison supplies practical efficiency evidence absent from v2, and the DBLP study adds a concrete real-network illustration. These gains are limited: timing covers one scenario, and DBLP fixes K=8 and provides descriptive statistics without ground-truth recovery evaluation. The unchanged theory and original simulation results remain the paper's principal support.
